IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (عمر بن الخطاب): Al-Daraqutni transmits from Umar a report similar to requiring wudu after touch; another report says Umar kissed his wife and prayed without wudu, so Ibn Kathir says the former, if sound, may indicate recommendation. IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (الشافعي وأصحابه ومالك وأحمد بن حنبل): Requiring wudu after physical touch is the position of al-Shafi‘i and his followers, Malik, and the well-known position from Ahmad. IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (معاذ): In a report from Muadh, a man says he met a woman and did everything short of intercourse; Quran 11:114 was revealed, and the Prophet ordered him to perform wudu and pray, saying the ruling applies to all believers. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (الشافعي): Al-Shafiʿi has two views on touching a young girl, elderly woman, or unmarriageable female: it breaks ablution under the verse's general wording, or does not because desire is irrelevant to them. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (المروزي): Al-Marwazi prefers the unrestricted Shafiʿi view because the verse does not condition touch on desire, as also reflected by Companions and most Successors. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (author): Al-Qurtubi rejects the objection that the Prophet could not touch ʿAisha through clothing: the report expressly describes him as touching her, and the Sunnah specifies that touch without desire or intent does not invalidate ablution. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (author): The reports show that direct touch does not invalidate ablution for every person who touches; Qurtubi's rule distinguishes touch according to pleasure. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (أبو ثور): Abu Thawr holds that kissing, intimate contact, or touching one's wife does not require ablution; Qurtubi associates this with the Hanafi school. ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (أبو حنيفة): Abū Ḥanīfa reads the phrase as intercourse, not hand-touch; even a kiss with desire does not invalidate ablution in his school. IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (author): The report does not establish wudu for touching because Abu Layla did not meet Muadh, leaving a gap in the chain. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (أبو حنيفة): Abu Hanifa holds that touching does not invalidate ablution, even with desire; another qualification says it does if erection occurs. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (الشافعي): Al-Shafiʿi differed over touching close relatives or a young unrelated woman; his sounder view is that it does not invalidate ablution, like touching teeth, nails, or hair. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (الشافعي): Al-Shafiʿi does not invalidate the touched person's ablution when their private part is touched, since that person did not touch a locus of pleasure. {"id": "4:43/q22", "question": "When is water legally unavailable?", "turns_on": "The cited interpretations, reports, language arguments, and legal evidence differ.", "positions": [{"id": "4:43/q22/p1", "position": "Water is physically absent", "reasons": "QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (الحسن وعطاء): Al-Hasan and ʿAtaʾ say the explicit condition of finding no water bars everyone from tayammum when water is available; Abu ʿUmar says this would be sound without the majority view and transmitted reports. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (بعض من ألف في أحكام القرآن): A writer on Quranic rulings argues that because “water” is indefinite, tayammum is forbidden whenever any amount of water exists, mixed with other matter or alone. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (author): Qurtubi argues that “not finding water” means one must first seek it, and tayammum is a necessity purification like that of a woman with continuous bleeding. BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 (author): “Finding no water” includes being unable to use it, since what one is barred from using counts as unavailable. IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (عمران بن حصين): In a report in both Sahih collections, the Prophet asks a Muslim who sat apart from the prayer group why he did not pray; the man says he is junub and has no water, and the Prophet tells him that clean earth suffices. IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم): Ammar reports that the Prophet camped at Awlat al-Jaysh with Aisha; after her Dhafar-bead necklace was lost and water was unavailable until dawn, God granted tayammum.

{"id": "4:43/q23", "question": "Must one search for water before tayammum?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "4:43/q23/p1", "position": "A search is required", "reasons": "RAZI-FULL, d. 606 (الشافعي): Al-Shāfiʿī requires a fresh search for water when each prayer time begins after a person has prayed using tayammum, since not finding it implies prior searching. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (مالك): Malik's apparent position, shared by al-Shafi'i, makes searching for water a condition for valid tayammum. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (أبو حنيفة): Abu Hanifa and Qadi Abu Muhammad ibn Nasr hold that searching for water is not a condition of valid tayammum. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (author): Qurtubi prefers requiring a search: the verse's “not finding water” presupposes looking, and a substitute is usable only when inability to obtain the original is certain. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (أبو حنيفة): Abu Hanifa, his two companions, and al-Muzani allow tayammum before the prayer time because searching for water is not a condition, analogizing to voluntary prayer. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (أبو الفرج): Abu al-Faraj permits making up multiple missed prayers with one tayammum; this assumes water-search is not a condition, which Qurtubi rejects. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (مالك): Malik requires a separate tayammum for each obligatory prayer because the worshipper must seek water anew for each one. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (author): Qurtubi prefers a new tayammum for each prayer: God requires seeking water for each prayer, and tayammum is an incomplete necessity-purity that consensus says ends when water appears. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (مطرف): A transmission from Ibn al-Qasim through Abu Zayd, and reports from Mutarrif and Ibn al-Majishun, require repeating the second prayer forever because seeking water is a condition. IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (كثير من الفقهاء): Many jurists infer that a person without water must first search for it; tayammum becomes permissible after searching and not finding any. IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 (عائشة): Aisha reports in a sound collection that the Prophet stopped the party at al-Bayda or Dhat al-Jaysh to search for her lost necklace; they had no water, the verse of tayammum came down, and the necklace was found beneath her camel. IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 (author): Tayammum was legislated in year six during the expedition of al-Muraysiʿ, after the group found itself without water while searching for Aisha's lost necklace.
